title: Breathwork techniques to reduce stress
titleChinese: 能缓解压力的呼吸法技巧
paragraphs: Whether you've reached work or study burnout, you're going through relationship dramas, or you just feel weighed down by life in general, stress is something that's difficult to avoid. If only there were an easy and free way to alleviate it. Luckily, there is! Breathwork. Breathing is the first and last thing we do on this planet, and it's the simplest way we can alleviate stress and anxiety both immediately and long-term, when done properly. So, how can we reap the benefits?

It's about slowing down. "We all tend to hyperventilate, breathing too fast and not very effectively," says David Spiegel, professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford University in the US. One way to make our breathing more intentional is a technique called 'cyclic sighing', with a focus on prolonged exhalation. Begin with a deep inhale through your nose. Just when you think you're done, take a short, sharp breath to fully fill the lungs. Then, let out a slow and extended sigh to completely empty your lungs. A 2023 study published in PubMed by Spiegel and colleagues found that just five minutes a day of cyclic sighing improved mood and lowered anxiety.

For a more advanced method, try 'coherent breathing'. To do this, you want to find a comfortable position, with one hand on your belly, and the other on your chest. Inhale through your nose for about six seconds, making the hand on your belly rise by engaging your diaphragm. Then exhale for the same duration. The key is to keep your breath smooth and continuous. "Imagine your breath as a slow tide coming in and going out," says Guy Fincham, who leads a breathwork research lab at Brighton and Sussex Medical School in the UK. The A52 breath method is similar, except at the end of the exhalation, you hold your breath for a couple of seconds before breathing in again.

Slowing down our breathing works because it relaxes the sympathetic nervous system, which is responsible for the 'fight-or-flight' response and activates the parasympathetic nervous system, responsible for the body's 'rest-and-digest' functions. This calms the body. So, whenever you start to feel overwhelmed, remember that you have this easy and instant stress-reliever in your toolkit.
chineseParagraphs: 无论你是工作或学习倦怠，经历感情纠葛，还是只是感到生活压力重重，压力都是难以避免的。要是有一种简单免费的方法来缓解它就好了。幸运的是，确实有！那就是呼吸法。呼吸是我们在这个星球上做的第一件事也是最后一件事，如果方法得当，它是我们即能立刻也能长期缓解压力和焦虑的最简单方法。那么，我们如何从中获益呢？

关键在于放慢速度。“我们都倾向于呼吸过速，呼吸过快且效率不高，”美国斯坦福大学精神病学和行为科学教授大卫·斯皮格尔说。一种让我们呼吸更有意识的方法是被称为“循环叹息”的技巧，重点是延长呼气。首先用鼻子深吸一口气。就在你认为吸完的时候，再短促有力地吸一口，使肺部完全充满。然后，缓慢而延长地叹息，完全排空肺部。斯皮格尔及其同事于2023年发表在PubMed上的一项研究发现，每天仅五分钟的循环叹息就能改善情绪并降低焦虑。
对于更进阶的方法，可以尝试“谐振呼吸”。为此，你需要找到一个舒适的姿势，一只手放在腹部，另一只手放在胸部。用鼻子吸气约六秒钟，通过调动膈肌使腹部的手抬起。然后用同样的时长呼气。关键是保持呼吸平稳连续。“想象你的呼吸就像缓慢的潮水涨落，”英国布莱顿和苏塞克斯医学院呼吸研究实验室负责人盖伊·芬查姆说。A52呼吸法类似，不同之处在于呼气结束时，在再次吸气前屏住呼吸几秒钟。
放慢呼吸之所以有效，是因为它放松了负责“战斗或逃跑”反应的交感神经系统，并激活了负责身体“休息和消化”功能的副交感神经系统。这能使身体平静下来。所以，每当你开始感到不堪重负时，请记住，你的工具箱里就有这个简单即时的减压器。

vocabulary.definition: 倦怠，过度劳累（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: burnout /ˈbɜːnaʊt/ n. 倦怠，过度劳累（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Long hours and high stress can lead to burnout.
vocabulary.translation: 长时间工作和高压会导致倦怠。

vocabulary.definition: 被……压垮，被……困扰（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: weighed down by /ˌweɪd ˈdaʊn baɪ/ phr. 被……压垮，被……困扰（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She felt weighed down by all her responsibilities.
vocabulary.translation: 她感到被所有责任压垮了。

vocabulary.definition: 减轻，缓解（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: alleviate /əˈliːvieɪt/ v. 减轻，缓解（书面语）
vocabulary.example: This medicine should alleviate your symptoms.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药应该能缓解你的症状。

vocabulary.definition: 呼吸法，呼吸练习（专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: breathwork /ˈbreθwɜːk/ n. 呼吸法，呼吸练习（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Breathwork can help reduce stress and improve focus.
vocabulary.translation: 呼吸法可以帮助减轻压力，提高注意力。

vocabulary.definition: 获益，得到好处（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: reap the benefits /ˌriːp ðə ˈbenɪfɪts/ phr. 获益，得到好处（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: You will soon reap the benefits of regular exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 你很快会收获定期锻炼的好处。

vocabulary.definition: 呼吸过速，过度换气（医学术语）
vocabulary.entry: hyperventilate /ˌhaɪpəˈventɪleɪt/ v. 呼吸过速，过度换气（医学术语）
vocabulary.example: When people panic, they often hyperventilate.
vocabulary.translation: 当人们恐慌时，常常会呼吸过速。

vocabulary.definition: 精神病学（医学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: psychiatry /saɪˈkaɪətri/ n. 精神病学（医学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Psychiatry is the branch of medicine that deals with mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 精神病学是处理心理健康的医学分支。

vocabulary.definition: 行为科学（专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: behavioural sciences /bɪˈheɪvjərəl ˈsaɪənsɪz/ n. 行为科学（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Behavioural sciences study how people and animals act.
vocabulary.translation: 行为科学研究人和动物的行为方式。

vocabulary.definition: 有意的，故意的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: intentional /ɪnˈtenʃənl/ adj. 有意的，故意的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She made an intentional effort to be kinder.
vocabulary.translation: 她有意努力变得更友善。

vocabulary.definition: 循环叹息（呼吸法专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: cyclic sighing /ˈsaɪklɪk ˈsaɪɪŋ/ n. 循环叹息（呼吸法专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Cyclic sighing involves deep inhales followed by prolonged exhales.
vocabulary.translation: 循环叹息包括深呼吸，然后延长呼气。

vocabulary.definition: 延长的，持久的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: prolonged /prəˈlɒŋd/ adj. 延长的，持久的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Prolonged use of the drug can be harmful.
vocabulary.translation: 长期使用这种药物可能有害。

vocabulary.definition: 呼气，呼出（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: exhalation /ˌekshəˈleɪʃn/ n. 呼气，呼出（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Focus on your exhalation during the breathing exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 在呼吸练习中专注于呼气。

vocabulary.definition: 吸入，吸气（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: inhale /ɪnˈheɪl/ v. 吸入，吸气（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He inhaled deeply before diving into the water.
vocabulary.translation: 他深吸一口气，然后跳入水中。

vocabulary.definition: 肺部（复数）
vocabulary.entry: lungs /lʌŋz/ n. 肺部（复数）
vocabulary.example: Smoking damages your lungs.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会损害你的肺部。

vocabulary.definition: 谐振呼吸（呼吸法专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: coherent breathing /kəʊˌhɪərənt ˈbriːðɪŋ/ n. 谐振呼吸（呼吸法专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Coherent breathing involves inhaling and exhaling for the same duration.
vocabulary.translation: 谐振呼吸包括相同时长的吸气和呼气。

vocabulary.definition: 腹部，肚子（口语）
vocabulary.entry: belly /ˈbeli/ n. 腹部，肚子（口语）
vocabulary.example: She was lying on her belly on the grass.
vocabulary.translation: 她趴在草地上。

vocabulary.definition: 横膈膜（解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: diaphragm /ˈdaɪəfræm/ n. 横膈膜（解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Singers are taught to breathe using their diaphragm.
vocabulary.translation: 歌手被教导使用横膈膜呼吸。

vocabulary.definition: 持续时间，期间（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: duration /djuˈreɪʃn/ n. 持续时间，期间（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The duration of the flight is about three hours.
vocabulary.translation: 航班的持续时间约为三个小时。

vocabulary.definition: 连续的，持续的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: continuous /kənˈtɪnjuəs/ adj. 连续的，持续的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The rain was continuous for three days.
vocabulary.translation: 雨连续下了三天。

vocabulary.definition: 潮水，潮汐
vocabulary.entry: tide /taɪd/ n. 潮水，潮汐
vocabulary.example: The tide was coming in, covering the sand.
vocabulary.translation: 涨潮了，淹没了沙滩。

vocabulary.definition: 交感神经系统（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: sympathetic nervous system /ˌsɪmpəˈθetɪk ˈnɜːvəs ˌsɪstəm/ n. 交感神经系统（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The sympathetic nervous system prepares the body for action.
vocabulary.translation: 交感神经系统让身体做好行动准备。

vocabulary.definition: 战或逃反应（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: fight-or-flight response /ˌfaɪt ɔː ˈflaɪt rɪˌspɒns/ n. 战或逃反应（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The fight-or-flight response prepares the body to deal with danger.
vocabulary.translation: 战或逃反应让身体准备好应对危险。

vocabulary.definition: 副交感神经系统（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: parasympathetic nervous system /ˌpærəˌsɪmpəˈθetɪk ˈnɜːvəs ˌsɪstəm/ n. 副交感神经系统（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The parasympathetic nervous system helps the body rest and digest.
vocabulary.translation: 副交感神经系统帮助身体休息和消化。

vocabulary.definition: 休息和消化（生理学术语）
vocabulary.entry: rest-and-digest /ˌrest ən ˈdaɪdʒest/ n. 休息和消化（生理学术语）
vocabulary.example: The parasympathetic nervous system is responsible for the rest-and-digest response.
vocabulary.translation: 副交感神经系统负责“休息和消化”反应。

vocabulary.definition: 不知所措的，被压垮的
vocabulary.entry: overwhelmed /ˌəʊvəˈwelmd/ adj. 不知所措的，被压垮的
vocabulary.example: She felt overwhelmed by the amount of work.
vocabulary.translation: 她被大量的工作压得喘不过气来。

vocabulary.definition: 工具箱（此处比喻可用的手段或方法）
vocabulary.entry: toolkit /ˈtuːlkɪt/ n. 工具箱（此处比喻可用的手段或方法）
vocabulary.example: You should have a toolkit of strategies to deal with stress.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该有一套应对压力的策略工具箱。
